note: Taking dependency 1.2 (p_i a <= p_i n_i for every i in {1,...,m}) as correct, this node sums the m inequalities termwise. Finitely many inequalities between reals may be added, since a <= b and c <= d imply a + c <= b + d, and this extends to any finite family by induction on m; the index set here is finite, so no convergence or rearrangement issue arises. This yields sum_{i=1}^m p_i a <= sum_{i=1}^m p_i n_i. The stated left-hand side, a sum_{i=1}^m p_i, is that same quantity with the constant factor a pulled out of the sum by distributivity — a is independent of i, being defined as the minimum over the whole index set, so the factorization is legitimate. The step invokes no property of the p_i beyond what 1.2 already delivered, and does not yet use sum_i p_i = 1, which is correctly deferred. Nothing is asserted here beyond finite additivity of <= plus distributivity.
